candidates.requirement: The XML_Parse surface must reach the supported disabled deferral setting and the enabled setting's deferred handling of repeated nonfinal partial-token input.
candidates.target_route: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput creates root, namespace and external-entity parsers; ParseOneInput configures handlers, then calls XML_Parse on the same full byte sequence once nonfinal and once final.
candidates.failure_condition: Every new parser starts with deferral enabled, child parsers inherit that value, and the target never calls XML_SetReparseDeferralEnabled. The sole later parse is final, so it cannot take the nonfinal deferral guard. No generated byte sequence can change those calls or the setting.
candidates.alternative_paths: Neither the namespace parser, child creation, reset, nor XML input supplies the missing configuration or an additional nonfinal call; all parsers follow the same fixed ParseOneInput sequence.

before.requirement: Selectable reparse deferral for repeated nonfinal partial-token parsing.
before.reason: The before XML_Parse routes directly to its processor, and the reconstructed before file has no deferral setter or callProcessor definition.

source_evidence.quote: Verified preimage file expat/lib/xmlparse.c has no function definition named XML_SetReparseDeferralEnabled. The entire after definition consists of added lines. This establishes absence in this file only; other implementations or equivalent paths must still be considered.

Verified preimage file expat/lib/xmlparse.c has no function definition named callProcessor. The entire after definition consists of added lines. This establishes absence in this file only; other implementations or equivalent paths must still be considered.

after.requirement: Reach selectable reparse deferral for repeated nonfinal partial-token parsing.
after.reason: The setter and deferral guard are supported, but the target retains the enabled default and calls XML_Parse only once nonfinally before a final call.

claims.reason: The same configurable-deferral tuple is assessed on both sides. It did not exist before; after the change, the fixed call sequence blocks it.
